macro_context.market_sentiment: Mixed and cautious on May 4: S&P 500 -0.13%, Dow -0.36%, Nasdaq +0.07% as US-Iran military tension flared (conflicting reports of attack on US warship) and oil spiked to $103.42. Broader context: S&P 500 and Nasdaq hit fresh all-time highs on May 1 (S&P 7,230; Nasdaq 25,114) lifted by Apple earnings beat, but geopolitical risk is now capping gains.
macro_context.fed_outlook: FOMC held benchmark rate at 3.5%-3.75% on April 29, 2026 (Powell's final meeting as chair) in an unusual 8-4 dissent vote. Markets pricing zero cuts in 2026 and one 25bp cut in December 2027. Inflation cited as elevated partly due to Middle East energy price surge; high uncertainty about the economic outlook.
macro_context.geopolitical: US-Iran military conflict is the dominant risk: Strait of Hormuz threats have pushed oil ~19% higher and rattled equity markets. IMF forecasts 3.1% global growth and 4.4% headline inflation even in a short-conflict scenario. Secondary risks include US-Venezuela tensions, NATO posturing in Greenland, and ongoing US tariff uncertainty.

web_context.competitor_activity: BYD is the dominant competitive threat globally: 2.26M pure EVs sold in 2025 vs Tesla's 1.64M (BYD up 28% YoY), targeting 1.3M overseas shipments in 2026 with new factories in Thailand, Brazil, and Hungary. Rivian beat Q1 2026 expectations but investors focused on cash burn; R3/R3X Model Y competitors expected under $50K. Ford and GM are scaling back EV ambitions, ceding ground to pure-plays. Tesla still holds >50% US EV market share.
